lines.label: Vehicle price
lines.help: Hammer or FOB price converted from JPY. Exporter fees and Japanese inland transport are extra (roughly ¥50,000 to ¥150,000).

lines.label: Shipping to Australia (RoRo)
lines.help: Roll-on roll-off to Melbourne, Sydney or Brisbane. Fremantle is at the high end. Containers cost more.
lines.note: Industry figures from Australian importers published in 2026, not official.

lines.label: Marine insurance
lines.help: Optional, but the border includes an insurance amount in the taxable value either way.
lines.note: Industry: 1.5% to 2% of value, about $350 minimum.

lines.label: Customs duty (JAEPA, Japanese-built)
lines.help: 0% for cars built in Japan under the Japan-Australia Economic Partnership Agreement. Must be claimed on the import declaration with an origin document; otherwise the general rate is 5%.
lines.note: Schedule 3 Ch.87 general rate 5% for used passenger cars; Schedule 11 (Japanese originating goods) lists no 87xx exception so rate is Free. Preference code JEPA.

lines.label: GST
lines.help: 10% of the value of the taxable importation: vehicle plus freight, insurance and duty.
lines.note: Paid to ABF before release from customs control.

lines.label: Luxury car tax
lines.help: 33% of the amount above the threshold, GST-exclusive. The LCT value includes freight, insurance, duty and GST. Applies on first import whatever the car's age.
lines.note: 2026-27 thresholds: $80,809 other vehicles, $91,661 fuel-efficient. Since 1 July 2025 fuel-efficient means 3.5 L/100 km combined or better, so petrol JDM cars use the lower threshold.

lines.label: ROVER import approval (older vehicle)
lines.help: Concessional RAV entry approval for 25+ year vehicles, includes the RAV charge. SEVS route is $95 plus $109 RAV charge instead.
lines.note: Fees document published May 2023 and still the linked schedule; confirm in ROVER at payment time.

lines.label: Port handling and customs broker
lines.help: Wharf and unloading fees plus a broker to lodge the import declaration.
lines.note: Industry ranges. ABF import processing and DAFF declaration charges are small and usually bundled.

lines.label: Biosecurity inspection and cleaning
lines.help: DAFF inspects used vehicles on arrival and charges per 15 minutes. Dirt, seeds or insects mean paid steam cleaning and re-inspection.
lines.note: Pre-export cleaning by a Recognised Offshore Cleaning Provider in Japan avoids most delays.

lines.label: Asbestos assurance
lines.help: Zero tolerance at the border for any age of vehicle. Pre-2000s cars are most at risk; test or replace gaskets, brake and clutch material before shipping and keep records.
lines.note: No official fee. Industry: $200 to $500 for basic pre-shipment testing, up to $3,500 for full test-and-certify packages.

lines.label: Compliance (older vehicle: roadworthy, VIN, engineer)
lines.help: 25+ year cars need no workshop modification, just state roadworthy and paperwork. Cars under 25 on the SEVS register need a Registered Automotive Workshop: budget $3,000 to $10,000 instead.
lines.note: Industry ranges, not official.

lines.label: First registration and CTP
lines.help: Varies by state. Excludes state stamp duty on first registration (roughly 3% to 4.2% of value), which can add thousands on a $50k car.
lines.note: Industry summary of state fees.

output.totalsNote: Excludes exporter commission, Japanese inland transport, state stamp duty and any repairs needed to pass roadworthy. Duty, GST and LCT follow official rates; other lines are typical market ranges.

lines.label: Vehicle price
lines.help: Hammer or FOB price converted from JPY. Customs counts exporter service and documentation fees as part of the price, so include them if you know them.

lines.label: Shipping to New Zealand (RoRo)
lines.help: Roll-on roll-off from Japan to Auckland, Wellington, Lyttelton or Nelson. Containers are roughly NZ$3,000 to NZ$4,500.
lines.note: No official figure. Industry ranges published in 2026 (jdmbuysell, tokyocarz, jpsheet). Excludes Japan-side inland transport and export documents.

lines.label: Marine insurance
lines.help: Optional. If paid, it is added to the value GST is charged on.
lines.note: Not an official rate. Exporters quote 1% to 2% of value.

lines.label: Pre-export cleaning and border inspection in Japan
lines.help: Used cars from Japan must be cleaned and inspected under an MPI-approved system (JEVIC, ATL, Bordercheck, KMA) before shipping. Paid in Japan.
lines.note: Industry estimate; mandatory, not optional.

lines.label: Customs duty
lines.help: Passenger cars are duty free in New Zealand whatever their origin. No origin certificate needed.
lines.note: Working Tariff Document Section XVII: all 87.03 'Other' passenger-car lines are Free. Only motorhomes and ambulances carry 10%.

lines.label: GST
lines.help: 15% of the vehicle value plus freight and insurance (duty is zero). Paid at import clearance before release.
lines.note: Customs may substitute an NZ-market valuation if the declared price looks unrealistically low. No depreciation allowance for a car bought remotely from NZ.

lines.label: Customs and MPI import levies
lines.help: Customs goods management levy plus MPI biosecurity levy on a sea import entry, including GST.

lines.label: Customs broker and port handling
lines.help: A broker lodges the import entry; the port charges wharf handling and documentation.
lines.note: Industry estimate: broker NZ$300 to NZ$700, port and documents NZ$100 to NZ$800.

lines.label: MPI biosecurity inspection on arrival
lines.help: NZ$99.60 per RoRo vehicle inspected at the port. A dirty car means re-inspection at NZ$178.83 an hour plus cleaning or heat treatment.
lines.note: Low end is the official per-vehicle fee ($86.61 excl GST). High end includes typical cleaning or BMSB-season heat treatment.

lines.label: Entry certification, transport and repairs
lines.help: An entry certifier checks frontal impact, emissions and ESC evidence and the car's condition. Private importers must trailer the car from the port. Repairs (tyres, brakes, glass, rust) are common.
lines.note: No official price and certifier price pages could not be read. Unverified industry estimate; confirm with VTNZ, VINZ or AA before launch.

lines.label: Clean Car Standard charge
lines.help: Every import needs a CO2 account, even a single private car. Pay-as-you-go used imports pay NZ$6 per g/km over a weight-adjusted 108 g/km target. Hybrids and EVs earn credits instead. Special interest vehicles are excluded.
lines.note: Depends on the car's CO2 figure: use the NZTA Clean Car Standard calculator for the exact charge. Rates set for 2026 and 2027; new used-import settings from 1 Jan 2028.

lines.label: First registration and licensing
lines.help: One-off registration with plates and 12 months licence, plus tyre, refrigerant, VIN and Clean Car admin fees. Diesel cars cost more and also pay road user charges.
lines.note: Official NZTA fees for a private petrol car from 1 July 2026: $311.22 (up to 1300cc) to $463.74 (4001cc+), plus $122.56 of first-registration extras.

output.totalsNote: Excludes exporter commission, Japanese inland transport and any repairs beyond typical entry-certification fixes. GST and levies follow official rates; other lines are typical market ranges.

lines.label: Vehicle price
lines.help: Hammer or FOB price converted from JPY. Duty is based on the price paid for the car. Exporter fees and Japanese inland transport are extra (roughly ¥50,000 to ¥150,000).

lines.label: Shipping to the US (RoRo)
lines.help: Roll-on roll-off to a West Coast port (Los Angeles, Oakland, Tacoma). East Coast ports (New York, New Jersey, Baltimore) cost more, roughly $2,000 to $4,200, and take about 45 days via the Panama Canal.
lines.note: Estimate from a US shipping company's published ranges (W.C. Shipping, March 2025; New York about $3,050 in their September 2026 guide). Not an official figure. Get a quote.

lines.label: Customs duty
lines.help: Japanese passenger cars 25+ years old: 2.5% normal duty plus the Section 301 tariff on Japanese goods (in force since 24 July 2026), 12.5% in total. Pickups and kei trucks: 25% (the long-standing truck rate; Section 301 adds nothing on top). Tariffs are changing fast and the 301 tariff is being challenged in court, so confirm with a licensed customs broker before you buy.
lines.note: CBP CSMS #69326983: products of Japan with a column 1 rate under 12.5% 'will be assessed a combined column one and Section 301 duty rate of 12.5%', effective 24 July 2026 (FR 2026-15181). MFN: 2.5% for heading 8703, 25% for 8704 (HTSUS Rev. 20, 2026). The Section 232 auto tariff does not apply to vehicles made in a year at least 25 years before entry (heading 9903.94.04). Whether those vehicles are also outside the Section 301 tariff is unclear: the notice exempts goods 'subject to tariffs under Section 232', and HTSUS note 52(f) does not list 9903.94.04 among the exempt headings, so 12.5% is used as the conservative estimate. If CBP treats them as exempt, passenger-car duty is 2.5%. Under the CIT challenge argued on 30 Sept 2026.

lines.label: Merchandise processing fee
lines.help: Charged by US Customs on every formal entry (any car worth over $2,500): 0.3464% of value, minimum $34.58, maximum $670.86 from 1 October 2026.
lines.note: FR 2026-15530: fiscal year 2027 figures, required from 1 Oct 2026; the 0.3464% rate is unchanged. Formal entry applies above $2,500 (19 CFR 143.21).

lines.label: Harbor maintenance fee
lines.help: 0.125% of the car's value for anything arriving by ship at a listed US port.
lines.note: 19 CFR 24.24: 'a port use fee of 0.125 percent (.00125) of its value'.

lines.label: Customs broker, entry bond and ISF filing
lines.help: A customs bond is required to release the car, and an Importer Security Filing must reach CBP at least 24 hours before a RoRo ship arrives (a late filing can cost $5,000). Most people pay a licensed broker to handle all three.
lines.note: Estimate: broker $400-$800 and single-entry bond $150-$500 (W.C. Shipping, Sep 2026), ISF filing about $25-$100 (secondary sources). Bond required by 19 CFR 142.4; ISF for RoRo per CBP ISF FAQ 2.0 (2023) and 19 CFR 149.

lines.label: Port and terminal handling
lines.help: Destination port, terminal and wharfage charges. If Customs picks the car for an exam, add roughly $1,000 to $2,000.
lines.note: Estimate from a US shipping company (March 2025). Exam costs are from secondary sources only.

output.totalsNote: Excludes exporter commission and Japanese inland transport, state sales or use tax (0% to about 10% depending on the state), title and registration, insurance, and any Gas Guzzler Tax (see below). Every line is an estimate; tariffs in particular are changing fast.
